summary:
H.R. 8752, the “Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2025,” makes FY2025 appropriations for DHS accounts, generally through September 30, 2025 unless expressly extended, and imposes account-specific conditions, transfer authorities, reporting requirements, and funding limitations.

Title I appropriates for Departmental Management, Intelligence, Situational Awareness, and Oversight, including the Office of the Secretary and Executive Management, Management Directorate, Intelligence, Analysis, and Situational Awareness, and the Office of Inspector General. Sections 101–106 require reports on noncompetitive awards, monthly budget and staffing reports, notification before Treasury Forfeiture Fund transfers under 31 U.S.C. 9705(g)(4)(B), quarterly acquisition briefings, and documentation and reporting before obligating funds for specified new pilots or demonstrations.

Title II funds Security, Enforcement, and Investigations, including CBP, ICE, TSA, Coast Guard, and Secret Service. It appropriates, inter alia, $16.566 billion for CBP Operations and Support, $1.390 billion for CBP Procurement, Construction, and Improvements, $10.497 billion for ICE Operations and Support, $10.817 billion for TSA Operations and Support, $10.554 billion for Coast Guard Operations and Support, $2.129 billion for Coast Guard Procurement, Construction, and Improvements, and $3.018 billion for Secret Service Operations and Support, with specified multi-year availability, fee offsets, trust fund derivations, and transfer authority. Sections 201–251 impose numerous limitations and directives, including CBP expenditure-plan submission before obligation (§208), allocation of CBP procurement funds including $600 million for physical barriers and obligation within 120 days (§211), restrictions on dismantling border barriers (§212), use of CBP One for parole (§213), certain admissions and parole authorities (§§215–216), ICE detention and 287(g) requirements and limitations (§§218–231), TSA screening and capital fund provisions (§§234–236), Coast Guard reporting and operational restrictions (§§237–244), Secret Service reimbursable protection and reprogramming provisions (§§245–248), and Coast Guard TRICARE contraceptive coverage provisions effective 30 and 180 days after enactment (§§250–251).

Title III appropriates for CISA and FEMA, including $2.437 billion for CISA Operations and Support, FEMA operations, $3.759 billion for Federal Assistance grant programs, $22.741 billion for the Disaster Relief Fund designated as disaster relief under BBEDCA §251(b)(2)(D), and National Flood Insurance Fund amounts derived from offsetting collections. Sections 301–311 govern cybersecurity threat-feed access, grant administrative caps and deadlines, FEMA award notice and rescission consequences, Stafford Act and fire-grant waivers, radiological preparedness fees, and transfers of prior mitigation and flood-mapping balances.

Title IV funds USCIS E-Verify, FLETC, the Science and Technology Directorate, and the Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Office, and includes USCIS vehicle and biometrics authorities, asylum- and employment-authorization funding limitations, discretionary FY2025 H-2B cap increase authority notwithstanding 8 U.S.C. 1184(g)(1)(B), FLETC accreditation and construction-transfer authorities, and prohibition on implementing the USCIS asylum program fee (§§401–413).

Title V contains government-wide DHS general provisions on availability, prior-year balance transfers, reprogramming and transfer thresholds (§§501–505), intelligence authorization treatment (§506), award notifications (§507), construction prospectus limits, Buy American compliance, reporting, congressional access to alien detention facilities, restraints on pregnant detainees, record preservation, unfunded-priority and protection reporting, Technology Modernization Fund conditions, southwest-border arrival estimates, and other funding prohibitions. It rescinds $600 million in prior CBP border-barrier balances and $154 million from the DHS Nonrecurring Expenses Fund (§§550–551), establishes a $10 million spending reduction account (§552), and includes additional limitations in §§553–567.
